name: Bird of Paradise
hook: No flowers yet? Your bird of paradise needs more sun.

steps.title: As much sun as you can
steps.tip: Put it by a big sunny window. It needs nearly full sun in summer and all the light it can get in winter.

steps.title: Moist summer, dry winter
steps.tip: Water well in spring and summer, but never soggy. From late autumn, let it get fairly dry between waterings.

steps.title: Keep it above 10–12°C
steps.tip: Bring it in before frost. If it spends summer outside, move it into stronger sun slowly to avoid sunburn.

steps.title: Feed every 2 weeks
steps.tip: Use liquid houseplant fertilizer every 2 weeks in spring and summer, then about once a month in winter.

steps.title: Repot only when full
steps.tip: When roots fill the pot, repot in spring into a slightly bigger one. Swap the top 5 cm of soil each spring.

steps.title: Wipe leaves, check pests
steps.tip: Wipe leaves with a soft cloth (no leaf shine) and check for mealybugs, scale and spider mites.

outro: Bright sun and patience: flowers can take 5–10 years to appear.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture Extension: Bird of Paradise, Strelitzia reginae
NC State Plant Toolbox: Strelitzia reginae

faqs.question: Why hasn't my bird of paradise flowered?
faqs.answer: It may simply be too young. Plants usually need to be 5–10 years old before they flower, and they need lots of bright light.
